# SMA-864: do not run tool calls from a turn that ended with `Length` or `ContentFilter`

Status: draft (2026-11-26). Linear: SMA-864. Size: a small change.

## 1. Intent

The agent loop runs every `Item::ToolCall` in a model turn. It does not look at
the finish reason. When `max_tokens` cuts a turn inside a `tool_use` block, the
Anthropic and Bedrock translators give a named call with `""` arguments. Core
changes `""` to `{}` (`crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/model.rs`, the
`args_str.trim().is_empty()` rule). The loop then runs the tool with `{}`. The
model did not mean that input.

A content filter can also stop a turn while a tool call is open. The arguments
of that call are not reliable either.

## 2. Rule

When a model turn in the `CallingModel` state has one or more `Item::ToolCall`
items **and** its `finish_reason` is `FinishReason::Length` or
`FinishReason::ContentFilter`, the loop:

1. runs **no** tool call and **no** handoff from that turn (the check comes
   before the handoff check, because a transfer call can be cut too);
2. emits `AgentEvent::MessageOutput` for each `Item::AssistantMessage` of the
   turn, in item order, as the other arms do;
3. emits `AgentEvent::RunFailed { error }`, where `error` is the `Display` text
   of the new error;
4. goes to `LoopState::Failed(AgentError::ToolCallsNotRun { .. })` with
   `NextAction::Terminate`.

The rule applies to the whole turn. If a `Length` turn has two complete calls
and a third cut call, the loop runs none of them, because one turn's calls are
one unit.

All other finish reasons keep today's behavior. This includes `Stop` and
`Other(_)` with tool calls: the tool calls run.

## 3. New public API

```rust
/// The model turn ended with a finish reason that makes its tool calls
/// unreliable (`Length` or `ContentFilter`), so the loop did not run them.
#[error("tool calls not run: the model turn ended with {finish_reason:?} ({tool_names:?})")]
ToolCallsNotRun {
    /// Why the model turn stopped.
    finish_reason: FinishReason,
    /// The names of the tool calls that did not run, in call order.
    tool_names: Vec<String>,
},
```

`AgentError` is `#[non_exhaustive]`, so the new variant is an additive change.
The exact `#[error]` text is the builder's call.

## 4. Approaches

- **Chosen: a guard arm in the pure `transition` function**
  (`crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/loop_state.rs`). The local driver
  (`agent.rs`) and the Temporal driver (`runtime-temporal/src/driver.rs`) both
  call `transition`, so one change covers both runners.
- Rejected: a check in the `agent.rs` driver. The Temporal runner would still
  run the cut calls.
- Rejected: a check in each provider. That puts a loop rule into six crates,
  and a new provider can forget it.
- Rejected: run tool calls only for `FinishReason::ToolCalls` (an allow-list).
  OpenAI Chat maps `function_call` to `Other("function_call")`, and many
  OpenAI-compatible servers behind LiteLLM send `"stop"` with valid tool calls.
  An allow-list would stop those runs.
- Rejected (Sven chose option 1): do not run the calls, send an error result
  for each call, and call the model again. The next turn has the same token
  limit, so this can repeat until `max_turns`.

## 5. Non-goals

- `Length` or `ContentFilter` **without** a tool call does not change. The run
  ends with the text it has.
- The `Finalizing` and `RepairingOutput` states do not change. They already
  treat any tool call as a validation failure.
- The failed state carries no token usage. No `LoopState::Failed` arm keeps
  usage today; this arm does the same.
- The Temporal runtime keeps its error mapping. `ErrorKindPayload::from_agent_error`
  maps an unknown variant to `Other { message }`, which is lossy but correct. A
  typed Temporal payload is a separate change if someone needs it.
- No provider changes. OpenAI `finish_reason: "length"` with partial arguments
  can also give a JSON parse error before the loop sees the turn; that path
  does not change.

## 6. Tests

- Unit test in `loop_state.rs`: `CallingModel` + `ModelResponse` with one
  `ToolCall` and `FinishReason::Length` gives `LoopState::Failed(ToolCallsNotRun
  { finish_reason: Length, tool_names: ["<name>"] })`, `NextAction::Terminate`,
  and a last event `RunFailed`. This is the acceptance-criteria test.
- The same for `FinishReason::ContentFilter`.
- A `Length` turn whose only tool call is a handoff transfer call: no
  `ApplyingHandoff`; the run fails.
- A regression test that `Stop` with a tool call still goes to
  `ExecutingTools`, so nobody changes the rule into an allow-list.
- An end-to-end test through the driver (a scripted model that returns a cut
  tool call with `Length`): the tool body never runs, and the run returns
  `AgentError::ToolCallsNotRun`.

## 7. Docs

- The new variant needs a `///` comment (`missing_docs`).
- The builder checks `docs/book/src/` for a page that lists `AgentError`
  variants or describes finish reasons, and updates it if one exists. The
  `paigasus-helikon-core` README needs an edit only if it lists error variants.
- A `CHANGELOG` is written by release-plz; no hand edit.

## 8. Left to the builder

- The exact `#[error]` text.
- Where the guard arm sits (it must match before the tool-call arm and after
  the max-turns arm).

1	//! Explicit state machine for the agent loop.
2	//!
3	//! Per ADR *"Explicit `LoopState` enum, not a callback maze"*, the
4	//! state machine is data: a pure [`transition`] function takes the
5	//! current state plus the most recent input and returns the next
6	//! state, the events to emit, and the side effect to perform. Durable
7	//! runners (Temporal, AgentCore in later tickets) reuse the same
8	//! function with their own driver.
9	
10	use crate::{
11	    AgentError, AgentEvent, ContentPart, FinishReason, Item, ModelRequest, ModelSettings,
12	    ResponseFormat, TokenUsage, ToolDef,
13	};
14	
15	/// The explicit, observable state of the agent loop.
16	///
17	/// One variant per high-level phase. Does **not** derive `Clone`:
18	/// `Failed(AgentError)` wraps `anyhow::Error` (not `Clone`). The
19	/// transition function takes input and returns outcome by value; tests
20	/// use `assert_matches!` on `next_state` instead of equality.
21	#[derive(Debug)]
22	#[non_exhaustive]
23	pub enum LoopState {
24	    /// About to call the model for turn `turn`.
25	    CallingModel {
26	        /// Zero-indexed turn counter.
27	        turn: u32,
28	        /// Cumulative token usage of all model turns completed before turn
29	        /// `turn` (SMA-402); `default()` at turn 0. Folded forward on every
30	        /// transition; the terminal `Done` / `RunCompleted` carry the grand total.
31	        usage: TokenUsage,
32	    },
33	    /// The model produced tool calls; about to execute them. `turn` is
34	    /// the turn that produced the calls — the next [`LoopState::CallingModel`]
35	    /// state will be `turn + 1`.
36	    ExecutingTools {
37	        /// The tool calls to execute concurrently.
38	        calls: Vec<ToolCallRequest>,
39	        /// The turn that produced these calls.
40	        turn: u32,
41	        /// Cumulative token usage of all model turns completed so far —
42	        /// including the turn that produced these calls (SMA-402). Carried
43	        /// forward unchanged across tool execution (tools add no tokens).
44	        usage: TokenUsage,
45	    },
46	    /// Handing off to another agent; carries the threaded transcript and the
47	    /// cumulative usage of all turns completed before the handoff (SMA-324).
48	    ApplyingHandoff {
49	        /// Name of the target agent.
50	        target: String,
51	        /// Conversation transcript to hand off.
52	        transcript: Vec<Item>,
53	        /// Cumulative usage of turns completed before the handoff.
54	        usage: TokenUsage,
55	    },
56	    /// Compacting session history. **Not driveable in SMA-314.**
57	    Compacting,
58	    /// Terminal: the run stopped on deferred tool calls that need a later
59	    /// decision. The full data of each call travels in
60	    /// [`AgentEvent::RunDeferred`]. Any input on this state fails.
61	    NeedsApproval {
62	        /// The tool calls awaiting approval.
63	        pending: Vec<ToolCallRequest>,
64	    },
65	    /// Constrained finalizing turn: the model is asked to emit the
66	    /// structured output for the configured `output_type`.
67	    Finalizing {
68	        /// The turn index that produced this finalizing request.
69	        turn: u32,
70	        /// Cumulative token usage of all model turns completed so far,
71	        /// including the turn that triggered finalizing (SMA-402).
72	        usage: TokenUsage,
73	    },
74	    /// The one allowed repair turn after a failed finalizing validation.
75	    RepairingOutput {
76	        /// The turn index of the finalizing turn being repaired.
77	        turn: u32,
78	        /// Cumulative token usage of all model turns completed so far,
79	        /// including the failed finalizing turn (SMA-402).
80	        usage: TokenUsage,
81	    },
82	    /// Terminal: run completed successfully.
83	    Done(FinalOutput),
84	    /// Terminal: run failed.
85	    Failed(AgentError),
86	}
87	
88	/// One tool call the model has requested. Pure data.
89	#[derive(Debug, Clone, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
90	pub struct ToolCallRequest {
91	    /// The provider-assigned call id (echoed back in `Item::ToolResult`).
92	    pub call_id: String,
93	    /// Tool name (matches [`crate::Tool::name`]).
94	    pub name: String,
95	    /// JSON-encoded arguments object.
96	    pub args: serde_json::Value,
97	}
98	
99	/// Outcome of one tool execution. Errors are stringified so the
100	/// outcome implements `Clone` — `ToolError` carries `anyhow::Error`,
101	/// which is not `Clone`.
102	#[derive(Debug, Clone, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
103	pub struct ToolCallOutcome {
104	    /// The call id this outcome corresponds to.
105	    pub call_id: String,
106	    /// Either the tool's content output or a stringified error.
107	    pub result: Result<Vec<ContentPart>, String>,
108	}
109	
110	/// Final assistant content + aggregated token usage at termination.
111	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
112	#[non_exhaustive]
113	pub struct FinalOutput {
114	    /// The terminal assistant content.
115	    pub content: Vec<ContentPart>,
116	    /// Aggregated token usage across all turns.
117	    pub usage: TokenUsage,
118	}
119	
120	impl FinalOutput {
121	    /// Concatenate all `ContentPart::Text` parts. This is the
122	    /// canonical rendering that feeds `RunResult.final_output` when
123	    /// `T = String`.
124	    pub fn as_text(&self) -> String {
125	        self.content
126	            .iter()
127	            .filter_map(|p| match p {
128	                ContentPart::Text { text } => Some(text.as_str()),
129	                _ => None,
130	            })
131	            .collect::<Vec<_>>()
132	            .join("")
133	    }
134	}
135	
136	/// Data fed *into* the next [`transition`] call.
137	#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
138	#[non_exhaustive]
139	pub enum TransitionInput {
140	    /// Seeds the loop with the initial conversation.
141	    Start {
142	        /// The user's input messages.
143	        messages: Vec<Item>,
144	    },
145	    /// One model turn aggregated.
146	    ModelResponse {
147	        /// Items produced this turn (assistant message + tool calls).
148	        items: Vec<Item>,
149	        /// Token usage for this turn.
150	        usage: TokenUsage,
151	        /// Why the model stopped emitting tokens.
152	        finish_reason: FinishReason,
153	    },
154	    /// All tool calls for one turn have completed.
155	    ToolResults {
156	        /// Per-call outcomes.
157	        outcomes: Vec<ToolCallOutcome>,
158	    },
159	    /// The tool calls of one turn have completed, and one or more calls were
160	    /// deferred. The run stops at this turn boundary.
161	    ToolResultsWithDeferrals {
162	        /// Per-call outcomes of the calls that ran (or failed), in call order.
163	        outcomes: Vec<ToolCallOutcome>,
164	        /// The deferred calls. `deferred` are the event copies, already redacted.
165	        deferred: Vec<crate::PendingToolCall>,
166	    },
167	}
168	
169	/// Side effect the async driver must run before the next transition.
170	#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
171	#[non_exhaustive]
172	pub enum NextAction {
173	    /// Call the model with this request; produce a `ModelResponse`.
174	    CallModel {
175	        /// The request to send.
176	        request: ModelRequest,
177	    },
178	    /// Execute these tool calls concurrently; produce a `ToolResults`, or a
179	    /// `ToolResultsWithDeferrals` when one or more calls were deferred.
180	    ExecuteTools {
181	        /// The calls to fan out.
182	        calls: Vec<ToolCallRequest>,
183	    },
184	    /// The current state is terminal; stop driving.
185	    Terminate,
186	    /// Delegate to a handoff target. The driver reads the target, transcript,
187	    /// and pre-handoff usage from the [`LoopState::ApplyingHandoff`] state.
188	    Handoff,
189	}
190	
191	/// What [`transition`] needs to know about the agent and config for
192	/// one step. Doesn't carry user `Ctx` — that's the driver's concern.
193	pub struct TransitionCtx<'a> {
194	    /// Tool definitions available this run.
195	    pub tools: &'a [ToolDef],
196	    /// Provider-tuning knobs.
197	    pub model_settings: &'a ModelSettings,
198	    /// Maximum number of turns before the loop fails.
199	    pub max_turns: u32,
200	    /// The driver's accumulated conversation so far. The driver
201	    /// appends incoming items before calling [`transition`] and passes
202	    /// the slice in — [`transition`] reads but never mutates.
203	    pub conversation: &'a [Item],
204	    /// Structured-output type, when the agent configured one. Drives the
205	    /// constrained finalizing turn and output validation.
206	    pub output: Option<&'a crate::OutputType>,
207	    /// Synthetic transfer-tool descriptors, one per handoff candidate. Empty
208	    /// when the agent has no handoffs.
209	    pub handoffs: &'a [crate::HandoffDef],
210	}
211	
212	/// One transition step's result. Not `Clone` (carries `LoopState`).
213	#[derive(Debug)]
214	pub struct TransitionOutcome {
215	    /// The state after this step.
216	    pub next_state: LoopState,
217	    /// Events to yield through the driver's event stream.
218	    pub events: Vec<AgentEvent>,
219	    /// Side effect the driver must run before the next step.
220	    pub next_action: NextAction,
221	    /// Items the driver must append to its owned conversation before the
222	    /// next step (e.g. a synthesized repair message). Empty in most arms.
223	    pub conversation_appends: Vec<Item>,
224	}
225	
226	/// Pure state-machine step. **No async, no tokio, no IO.**
227	///
228	/// Given the current state and the most recent input, produce the
229	/// next state, the events to emit, and the side effect to perform.
230	/// Resumable by construction: a durable runner can persist
231	/// [`LoopState`] plus the accumulated conversation and rehydrate the
232	/// loop at any transition boundary.
233	pub fn transition(
234	    state: &LoopState,
235	    input: TransitionInput,
236	    ctx: &TransitionCtx<'_>,
237	) -> TransitionOutcome {
238	    match (state, input) {
239	        // Max turns reached at the CallingModel boundary → fail fast.
240	        (LoopState::CallingModel { turn, .. }, _) if *turn >= ctx.max_turns => TransitionOutcome {
241	            next_state: LoopState::Failed(AgentError::MaxTurnsExceeded(ctx.max_turns)),
242	            events: vec![AgentEvent::RunFailed {
243	                error: format!("max turns ({}) exceeded", ctx.max_turns),
244	            }],
245	            next_action: NextAction::Terminate,
246	            conversation_appends: Vec::new(),
247	        },
248	        // Start seeds the loop: emit TurnStarted, request CallModel.
249	        (LoopState::CallingModel { turn, usage: prior }, TransitionInput::Start { .. })
250	            if *turn < ctx.max_turns =>
251	        {
252	            match ctx.output {
253	                Some(out) if ctx.tools.is_empty() => {
254	                    let request = ModelRequest {
255	                        messages: ctx.conversation.to_vec(),
256	                        tools: Vec::new(),
257	                        model_settings: constrained_settings(ctx.model_settings, out),
258	                    };
259	                    TransitionOutcome {
260	                        next_state: LoopState::Finalizing {
261	                            turn: *turn,
262	                            usage: *prior,
263	                        },
264	                        events: vec![AgentEvent::TurnStarted { turn: *turn }],
265	                        next_action: NextAction::CallModel { request },
266	                        conversation_appends: Vec::new(),
267	                    }
268	                }
269	                _ => {
270	                    let request = ModelRequest {
271	                        messages: ctx.conversation.to_vec(),
272	                        tools: turn_tools(ctx),
273	                        model_settings: ctx.model_settings.clone(),
274	                    };
275	                    TransitionOutcome {
276	                        next_state: LoopState::CallingModel {
277	                            turn: *turn,
278	                            usage: *prior,
279	                        },
280	                        events: vec![AgentEvent::TurnStarted { turn: *turn }],
281	                        next_action: NextAction::CallModel { request },
282	                        conversation_appends: Vec::new(),
283	                    }
284	                }
285	            }
286	        }
287	        // Model produced tool calls → fan out to ExecutingTools.
288	        (
289	            LoopState::CallingModel { turn, usage: prior },
290	            TransitionInput::ModelResponse { items, usage, .. },
291	        ) if items.iter().any(|i| matches!(i, Item::ToolCall { .. })) => {

295	                    .handoffs
296	                    .iter()

298	                    .map(|h| h.target.clone()),
299	                _ => None,
300	            }) {

302	                let mut events: Vec<AgentEvent> = Vec::new();
303	                for item in &items {
304	                    match item {
305	                        Item::AssistantMessage { .. } => {
306	                            events.push(AgentEvent::MessageOutput { item: item.clone() });
307	                        }
308	                        Item::ToolCall { name, .. }

310	                        {

318	                        target,
319	                        transcript: thread_handoff_transcript(ctx.conversation),
320	                        usage: total,

322	                    events,

324	                    conversation_appends: Vec::new(),

327	            // (existing ExecutingTools logic continues unchanged below)
328	            let mut events: Vec<AgentEvent> = Vec::new();

330	            for item in &items {

336	                        call_id,
337	                        name,
338	                        args,

521	/// [`Model`] in `RetryingModel` (with a `RetryPolicy`) from
522	/// `paigasus-helikon-runtime-tokio` to retry the transient variants
523	/// (`Unavailable`, `RateLimited`, `Transport`) with backoff.
524	#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
525	#[non_exhaustive]
526	pub enum ModelError {
527	    /// Provider returned a no-route / 503 / connection-refused style error.
528	    #[error("model provider unavailable")]
529	    Unavailable,
530	
531	    /// Provider rate-limited the request. `retry_after_ms` carries the
532	    /// provider's hint when one is supplied (e.g. via `Retry-After`).
533	    #[error("rate limited (retry after {retry_after_ms:?} ms)")]
534	    RateLimited {
535	        /// Provider-supplied retry hint in milliseconds.
536	        retry_after_ms: Option<u64>,
537	    },
538	
539	    /// Request exceeded the provider's context-length limit.
540	    #[error("context length exceeded")]
541	    ContextLengthExceeded,
542	
543	    /// Provider refused the request (content policy, account state, …).
544	    #[error("model refused: {reason}")]
545	    Refused {
546	        /// Human-readable reason supplied by the provider.
547	        reason: String,
548	    },
549	
550	    /// Transport-level failure (DNS, TLS, socket reset). The string is
551	    /// provider-formatted.
552	    #[error("transport error: {0}")]
553	    Transport(String),
554	
555	    /// Escape hatch for arbitrary upstream failures. See ADR-10.
556	    #[error(transparent)]
557	    Other(#[from] anyhow::Error),
558	}

560	// ── Model-turn accumulation ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
561	
562	/// One fully-aggregated model turn.
563	///
564	/// Reassembled from a [`ModelEvent`] stream by [`ModelTurnAccumulator`]: the
565	/// concatenated text/reasoning deltas become at most one
566	/// [`crate::Item::AssistantMessage`]. Provider data alone also creates that
567	/// message. Each distinct `ToolCallDelta` `call_id` becomes one
568	/// [`crate::Item::ToolCall`], `usage` is the last `Usage` snapshot observed,
569	/// and `finish_reason` is the terminal `Finish` reason.
570	/// Two or more blank-id calls make [`ModelTurnAccumulator::finish`] fail
571	/// instead of producing items.
572	#[derive(Debug, Clone, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
573	#[non_exhaustive]
574	pub struct ModelTurn {
575	    /// Reconstructed items: an optional leading `AssistantMessage` (reasoning,
576	    /// text and/or provider data content, in that order) followed by
577	    /// zero or more `ToolCall`s, in deterministic `call_id`-sorted order.
578	    pub items: Vec<crate::Item>,
579	    /// The last [`ModelEvent::Usage`] snapshot observed (last-wins; usage
580	    /// snapshots are never summed within a turn), or the zero default if
581	    /// the stream never emitted one.
582	    pub usage: crate::TokenUsage,
583	    /// Why the response ended.
584	    pub finish_reason: FinishReason,
585	}
586	
587	impl ModelTurn {
588	    /// Construct a `ModelTurn` directly from its parts.
589	    ///
590	    /// The normal path is [`ModelTurnAccumulator::finish`], which reassembles
591	    /// a turn from a live [`ModelEvent`] stream. This constructor is for
592	    /// callers that already have `items`/`usage`/`finish_reason` in hand —
593	    /// durable-runner activities that reconstruct a turn from a stored
594	    /// result, and tests — and would otherwise be unable to build one at all
595	    /// (`#[non_exhaustive]` blocks struct-literal construction outside this
596	    /// crate).
597	    pub fn new(
598	        items: Vec<crate::Item>,
599	        usage: crate::TokenUsage,
600	        finish_reason: FinishReason,
601	    ) -> Self {
602	        Self {
603	            items,
604	            usage,
605	            finish_reason,
606	        }
607	    }
608	}
609	
610	/// Accumulates the in-progress tool call across `ModelEvent::ToolCallDelta`
611	/// chunks for one `call_id`.
612	#[derive(Debug, Default)]
613	struct ToolCallAccum {
614	    name: Option<String>,
615	    args_str: String,
616	}
617	
618	/// Reassemble streamed model output into [`crate::Item`]s.
619	fn build_items(
620	    agent_name: &str,
621	    text: String,
622	    reasoning: String,
623	    provider_data: Vec<crate::ContentPart>,
624	    tool_accum: std::collections::BTreeMap<String, ToolCallAccum>,
625	) -> Result<Vec<crate::Item>, String> {
626	    let mut items = Vec::new();
627	    if !text.is_empty() || !reasoning.is_empty() || !provider_data.is_empty() {
628	        let mut content = Vec::new();
629	        if !reasoning.is_empty() {
630	            content.push(crate::ContentPart::Reasoning { text: reasoning });
631	        }
632	        if !text.is_empty() {
633	            content.push(crate::ContentPart::Text { text });
634	        }
635	        content.extend(provider_data);
636	        items.push(crate::Item::AssistantMessage {
637	            content,
638	            agent: Some(agent_name.to_owned()),
639	        });
640	    }
641	    for (call_id, accum) in tool_accum {
642	        // OpenAI streaming legitimately emits an empty `arguments` delta for
643	        // zero-parameter tool calls — normalize blank/whitespace-only args to
644	        // `{}` rather than failing the whole turn on a `serde_json` EOF error.
645	        let args_str = if accum.args_str.trim().is_empty() {
646	            "{}"
647	        } else {
648	            accum.args_str.as_str()
649	        };
650	        let args = serde_json::from_str(args_str).map_err(|e| {
651	            format!(
652	                "invalid tool args for call_id={call_id} (name={}): {e}",
653	                accum.name.as_deref().unwrap_or("?")
654	            )
655	        })?;
656	        items.push(crate::Item::ToolCall {
657	            call_id,
658	            name: accum.name.unwrap_or_default(),
659	            args,
660	        });
661	    }
662	    Ok(items)
663	}

665	/// Accumulates a streamed model response into a [`ModelTurn`].
666	///
667	/// Feed every successful [`ModelEvent`] from a [`Model::invoke`] stream via
668	/// [`Self::observe`], then call [`Self::finish`] once the stream ends (after
669	/// observing a `Finish` event) to reassemble the turn's [`crate::Item`]s.
670	#[derive(Debug)]
671	pub struct ModelTurnAccumulator {
672	    agent_name: String,
673	    text: String,
674	    reasoning: String,
675	    provider_data: Vec<crate::ContentPart>,
676	    tool_accum: std::collections::BTreeMap<String, ToolCallAccum>,
677	    /// Names carried by deltas under a blank `call_id`, in arrival order.
678	    blank_names: Vec<String>,
679	    finish_reason: FinishReason,
680	    latest_usage: Option<crate::TokenUsage>,
681	}
682	
683	impl ModelTurnAccumulator {
684	    /// Start a new accumulator. `agent_name` is attributed to the
685	    /// resulting turn's `AssistantMessage`, if any.
686	    pub fn new(agent_name: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
687	        Self {
688	            agent_name: agent_name.into(),
689	            text: String::new(),
690	            reasoning: String::new(),
691	            provider_data: Vec::new(),
692	            tool_accum: std::collections::BTreeMap::new(),
693	            blank_names: Vec::new(),
694	            finish_reason: FinishReason::Stop,
695	            latest_usage: None,
696	        }
697	    }
698	
699	    /// Feed one successful model event. `Err(ModelEvent)`s are the caller's
700	    /// concern — this only observes `Ok` events from the stream.
701	    pub fn observe(&mut self, event: &ModelEvent) {
702	        match event {
703	            ModelEvent::TokenDelta { text } => self.text.push_str(text),
704	            ModelEvent::ReasoningDelta { text } => self.reasoning.push_str(text),
705	            ModelEvent::ToolCallDelta {
706	                call_id,
707	                name,
708	                args_delta,
709	            } => {
710	                if call_id.is_empty() {
711	                    if let Some(n) = name {
712	                        self.blank_names.push(n.clone());
713	                    }
714	                }
715	                let a = self.tool_accum.entry(call_id.clone()).or_default();
716	                if a.name.is_none() {
717	                    if let Some(n) = name.as_deref() {
718	                        a.name = Some(n.to_owned());
719	                    }
720	                }
721	                a.args_str.push_str(args_delta);
722	            }
723	            ModelEvent::Usage {
724	                input_tokens,
725	                output_tokens,
726	                cached_input_tokens,
727	                reasoning_tokens,
728	            } => {
729	                self.latest_usage = Some(crate::TokenUsage {
730	                    input_tokens: u64::from(*input_tokens),
731	                    output_tokens: u64::from(*output_tokens),
732	                    cached_input_tokens: cached_input_tokens.map(u64::from).unwrap_or(0),
733	                    reasoning_tokens: reasoning_tokens.map(u64::from).unwrap_or(0),
734	                    total_tokens: u64::from(*input_tokens) + u64::from(*output_tokens),
735	                });
736	            }
737	            ModelEvent::Finish { reason } => {
738	                self.finish_reason = reason.clone();
739	            }
740	            ModelEvent::ProviderData {
741	                provider,
742	                call_id,
743	                data,
744	            } => self.provider_data.push(crate::ContentPart::ProviderData {
745	                provider: provider.clone(),
746	                call_id: call_id.clone(),
747	                data: data.clone(),
748	            }),
749	        }
750	    }
751	
752	    /// Reassemble. `Err(String)` = invalid JSON in accumulated tool-call
753	    /// args, **or** an ambiguous blank-id bucket (two or more name-carrying
754	    /// deltas under `""`), which is checked first, before any parse.
755	    pub fn finish(self) -> Result<ModelTurn, String> {
756	        if self.blank_names.len() >= 2 {
757	            let count = self.blank_names.len();
758	            let list = format_blank_names(&self.blank_names);
759	            tracing::warn!(
760	                target: "paigasus::core::model",
761	                count,
762	                names = %list,
763	                "refusing a model turn with parallel tool calls under a blank call_id"
764	            );
765	            return Err(format!(
766	                "ambiguous tool calls: {count} parallel tool calls arrived under a blank call_id (names: {list}); their arguments cannot be attributed to a call"
767	            ));
768	        }
769	        let items = build_items(
770	            &self.agent_name,
771	            self.text,
772	            self.reasoning,
773	            self.provider_data,
774	            self.tool_accum,
775	        )?;
776	        Ok(ModelTurn {
777	            items,
778	            usage: self.latest_usage.unwrap_or_default(),
779	            finish_reason: self.finish_reason,
780	        })
781	    }
782	}

784	/// Format at most 8 names, each cut to 64 chars and Debug-escaped.
785	fn format_blank_names(names: &[String]) -> String {
786	    const MAX_NAMES: usize = 8;
787	    const MAX_CHARS: usize = 64;
788	    let mut out = names
789	        .iter()
790	        .take(MAX_NAMES)
791	        .map(|n| format!("{:?}", n.chars().take(MAX_CHARS).collect::<String>()))
792	        .collect::<Vec<_>>()
793	        .join(", ");
794	    if names.len() > MAX_NAMES {
795	        out.push_str(&format!(", and {} more", names.len() - MAX_NAMES));
796	    }
797	    out
798	}

728	/// Build the terminal `[Usage, Finish]` event pair from a response's
729	/// usage snapshot, status, optional `incomplete_details.reason` string, and
730	/// whether the response produced any tool calls.
731	///
732	/// When `incomplete_reason` is `Some`, it overrides the status-based mapping:
733	/// - `"max_output_tokens"` → `Finish { Length }`
734	/// - `"content_filter"` → `Finish { ContentFilter }`
735	/// - other string → `Finish { Other(reason) }`
736	///
737	/// `has_tool_calls` only affects the `Status::Completed` arm of the
738	/// status-based mapping: real traffic confirms a turn whose sole output is a
739	/// function call still reports `status: "completed"` with
740	/// `incomplete_details: null` (see
741	/// `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-openai/tests/fixtures/responses_tool_call.txt`),
742	/// so `status` alone cannot tell a tool-call turn from an ordinary text
743	/// completion. The `ResponseIncomplete` caller passes `!item_to_call.is_empty()`
744	/// to resolve that; the `ResponseCompleted` caller passes
745	/// `!emitted_items.is_empty()` instead, evaluated after reconciling against
746	/// `response.output` — the two differ because that reconciliation step can
747	/// register a call into `item_to_call` (via `output_item.added`) that it never
748	/// actually emits (e.g. an item later found to be `Incomplete`), so only
749	/// `emitted_items` is guaranteed to track what was emitted (SMA-562).
750	/// Every other status arm ignores it, matching every other subject in the
751	/// stream conformance suite, which distinguish `ToolCalls` from `Stop` only
752	/// on the natural-completion path.
753	///
754	/// **Invariant (SMA-522):** `Usage` is constructed *only* here, and this
755	/// function unconditionally appends `Finish` before returning. That — not the
756	/// incidental fact that both derive from one event — is what keeps the
757	/// backend's ordering correct. A future arm emitting `Usage` elsewhere would
758	/// break it.
759	fn terminal_events(
760	    usage: Option<ResponseUsage>,
761	    status: Status,
762	    incomplete_reason: Option<&str>,
763	    has_tool_calls: bool,
764	) -> Vec<ModelEvent> {
765	    let mut out = Vec::new();
766	
767	    if let Some(u) = usage {
768	        out.push(ModelEvent::Usage {
769	            input_tokens: u.input_tokens,
770	            output_tokens: u.output_tokens,
771	            cached_input_tokens: Some(u.input_tokens_details.cached_tokens),
772	            reasoning_tokens: Some(u.output_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens),
773	        });
774	    }
775	
776	    let reason = if let Some(r) = incomplete_reason {
777	        match r {
778	            "max_output_tokens" => FinishReason::Length,
779	            "content_filter" => FinishReason::ContentFilter,
780	            other => FinishReason::Other(other.to_owned()),
781	        }
782	    } else {
783	        match status {

75	/// [`ModelTurnResult`].
76	///
77	/// SDK-free: unit-testable without a Temporal worker. A
78	/// [`paigasus_helikon_core::ModelError`] from either [`Model::invoke`]
79	/// itself or a stream-level event degrades to [`ErrorKindPayload::Model`]; a
80	/// successfully-drained stream that fails to reassemble (invalid
81	/// tool-call-argument JSON, or parallel tool calls under a blank `call_id`)
82	/// degrades to [`ErrorKindPayload::Other`].
83	pub(crate) async fn call_model_inner(
84	    model: &dyn Model,
85	    agent_name: &str,
86	    request: ModelRequest,
87	    cancel: CancellationToken,
88	) -> Result<ModelTurnResult, ErrorKindPayload> {
89	    use futures_util::StreamExt;
90	
91	    let mut stream = model
92	        .invoke(request, cancel)
93	        .await
94	        .map_err(|e| ErrorKindPayload::Model {
95	            message: e.to_string(),
96	        })?;
97	
98	    let mut acc = ModelTurnAccumulator::new(agent_name);
99	    while let Some(event) = stream.next().await {
100	        match event {
101	            Ok(ev) => acc.observe(&ev),
102	            Err(e) => {
103	                return Err(ErrorKindPayload::Model {
104	                    message: e.to_string(),
105	                });
106	            }
107	        }
108	    }
109	
110	    acc.finish()
111	        .map(ModelTurnResult)
112	        .map_err(|message| ErrorKindPayload::Other { message })
113	}

325	//! tool call, not once per run) — keep it small (ids, claims), not bulk data.
326	//!
327	//! Payload codecs (custom serialization), claim-check blob offloading, and conversation
328	//! compaction are named follow-up work, not silent gaps.
329	//!
330	//! # Upgrade Discipline and Determinism
331	//!
332	//! The workflow's deterministic core is [`paigasus_helikon_core::loop_state::transition`], which
333	//! lives in a separately versioned crate. Replaying an in-flight workflow against a worker with a
334	//! **different version of `paigasus-helikon-core` or `paigasus-helikon-runtime-temporal`** can
335	//! cause non-determinism errors (the workflow's replayed decisions don't match the new code's
336	//! logic).
337	//!
338	//! **Activity input encoding is not a replay hazard.** Temporal's replay check compares an
339	//! activity's **id** and **type** only — never its input payloads
340	//! (`temporalio-sdk-core-0.9.0`, `activity_state_machine.rs`, the
341	//! `IdAndTypeDeterminismChecks` gate). Changing how an activity's arguments are encoded
342	//! therefore cannot trip the non-determinism checker; *renaming* an activity would. This
343	//! statement is pinned to `temporalio-* = 1.0.0` / `temporalio-sdk-core = 0.9.0` and must
344	//! be re-verified on any SDK bump.
345	//! (Re-verified for 1.0 in SMA-622: `on_activity_task_scheduled` in
346	//! `temporalio-sdk-core-0.9.0` is byte-identical to the 0.7.0 body and still compares only
347	//! `act_id`/`activity_id` and `act_type`/`activity_type`, never payloads. Activity and
348	//! workflow *type names* are derived unchanged as well
349	//! (`temporalio-macros-1.0.0/src/activities_definitions.rs:548`,
350	//! `workflow_definitions.rs:644-647`), so registered names are stable across the bump —
351	//! which is what makes this guarantee useful rather than merely true.
352	//! Previously re-verified for 0.7 in SMA-549.)
353	//!
354	//! **A mixed 0.7/1.0 worker fleet is not proven safe.** The two properties above are
355	//! established: input encoding is not a replay hazard, and activity/workflow type names
356	//! do not move. Beyond them, nothing in CI exercises a 1.0 worker replaying a history
357	//! written by a 0.7 worker — `temporal-it` starts a fresh server, so it only ever replays
358	//! its own 1.0 histories. Prefer draining in-flight runs across this upgrade, or use a
359	//! blue-green task queue, exactly as for the 0.5.0 envelope change below.
360	//!
361	//! **SMA-484 wire change (activity inputs are envelope-only as of 0.3.0).** Each of
362	//! `render_instructions` / `call_model` / `invoke_tool` takes one self-describing JSON-object
363	//! payload, and that is now the **only** shape a worker decodes. The pre-envelope positional
364	//! shapes (0.2.1 and earlier) are recognized solely to produce a named decode error; SMA-462's
365	//! 0.2.2 release, which decoded both, is the migration bridge **for 0.2.0 and 0.2.1**. 0.1.x
366	//! remains outside the support window and fails closed as before — see the 0.1.x note below,
367	//! because the bridge does not rescue it.
368	//!
369	//! **Upgrading from 0.2.0 or 0.2.1 requires a stop at 0.2.2**, for activity inputs:
370	//!
371	//! | from → to | outcome |
372	//! |---|---|
373	//! | `0.2.2` → `0.3.0` | compatible **both** ways — both encode and decode the envelope; no drain needed for this change |
374	//! | `0.2.0` / `0.2.1` → `0.3.0`, directly | **broken both ways** — `0.3.0` cannot read legacy-queued tasks, and a `0.2.0`/`0.2.1` worker cannot read an envelope |
375	//! | `0.2.0` / `0.2.1` → `0.2.2` → `0.3.0` | works, **provided in-flight runs are drained while the fleet is on 0.2.2** |
376	//!
377	//! **0.1.x cannot use the bridge.** 0.2.2 decodes the 0.2.0/0.2.1 arities specifically, and only
378	//! `call_model`'s shape (2 payloads) happens to be unchanged since 0.1.x. A 0.1.x
379	//! `render_instructions` task is one payload and fails in 0.2.2's envelope arm; a 0.1.x
380	//! `invoke_tool` task is two payloads, which is not `invoke_tool`'s legacy arity, so it fails
381	//! there too. A fleet on 0.1.x must therefore drain (or terminate) its in-flight runs outright
382	//! rather than hopping through 0.2.2. Note the *diagnostic* wording stays "0.2.1 and earlier"
383	//! deliberately: it describes the shape that arrived, and `call_model`'s 2-payload shape really
384	//! does date back to 0.1.x.
385	//!
386	//! Throughout this section, *drain* means: stop starting new executions on the task queue, and
387	//! wait until every execution already on it reaches a **terminal** state — not merely pausing
388	//! new runs.
389	//!
390	//! **If a 0.3.0 worker meets a pre-envelope task anyway**, it logs at `ERROR` and fails the
391	//! attempt **retryably**, so Temporal re-dispatches. That is the recovery path: any worker on
392	//! 0.2.2 still polling the queue decodes and executes the task, for as long as 0.2.2 can still
393	//! decode the nested core types in play (see the field-evolution scope below). Re-join one, let
394	//! in-flight runs drain, then remove it. 0.2.2 and 0.3.0 share identical workflow logic, so a
395	//! temporary mixed fleet across this pair is not a replay hazard; the one-version-at-a-time rule
396	//! above still governs every other pair. A run that cannot be drained in an acceptable window is
397	//! handled with a blue-green task queue (below) or by terminating the execution.
398	//!
399	//! **The envelope is unreadable below 0.2.2, and that matters during a rolling deploy.** A
400	//! **0.2.1-and-earlier** worker handed an envelope payload cannot decode it. It fails the
401	//! attempt retryably and Temporal re-dispatches until a worker that understands the envelope
402	//! takes it. The same is true of a 0.3.0 worker handed a pre-envelope payload. Four things bound
403	//! that recovery:
404	//!
405	//! 1. A finite `maximum_attempts` on `model_retry_policy` / `tool_retry_policy` can be exhausted.
406	//! 2. `WorkflowInput::timeout_ms` interrupts the whole run on its own schedule, regardless of
407	//!    retry policy.
408	//! 3. A terminal `render_instructions` failure ends the run; it is not a degraded step.
409	//! 4. Exhausted `invoke_tool` retries are folded into a tool-error result and fed to the model
410	//!    rather than failing loudly.
411	//!
412	//! **Neither of the first two is on by default.** `render_instructions` is built with no retry
413	//! policy at all, so the Temporal server default — unlimited attempts — applies; and
414	//! `WorkflowInput::timeout_ms` is `None` unless set, meaning no deadline. On a default
415	//! configuration the retry loop is therefore **unbounded**: the run retries indefinitely, writing
416	//! one `ActivityTaskFailed` event per attempt and consuming workflow history. Do not rely on the
417	//! failure self-terminating; recovery is operator action.
418	//!
419	//! So: **keep the mixed-fleet window short**, and either drain in-flight runs first or ensure
420	//! retry caps are unlimited and run deadlines generous for the duration of the rollout.
421	//!
422	//! **Rolling back.** Once a worker has queued an envelope-shaped activity task, that payload is
423	//! frozen in the `ActivityTaskScheduled` event and every retry re-delivers it. A rollback to
424	//! **below 0.2.2** leaves those activities undecodable until the run deadline — which, on a
425	//! default configuration, does not exist. **Drain in-flight runs before rolling back below 0.2.2.**
426	//! Rolling back from 0.3.0 to 0.2.2 is safe: 0.2.2 decodes the envelope.
427	//!
428	//! **What this buys.** Future additive changes to an activity's input are compatible in both
429	//! directions, because the envelope is self-describing: unknown fields are ignored and absent
430	//! fields default. That guarantee is scoped to **the envelope's own field set**. It does *not*
431	//! extend to the `paigasus-helikon-core` types nested inside those envelopes (`ModelRequest`,
432	//! `ToolCallRequest`), nor to activity **outputs** — a serde change in any of those breaks the
433	//! wire exactly as before.
434	//!
435	//! **Operational guidance:**
436	//!
437	//! 1. **Upgrade one release at a time.** Skipping a release skips the overlap window in which
438	//!    both shapes are readable (a fleet on 0.2.0 or 0.2.1 goes → 0.2.2 → 0.3.0, draining while
439	//!    on 0.2.2; 0.1.x has no such overlap and must drain outright).
440	//! 2. **Drain in-flight runs before redeploying** when in doubt. Agent runs are typically
441	//!    minutes-to-hours, not months. Alternatively use blue-green task queues: point the old
442	//!    worker to `"queue-v1"` and the runner to `"queue-v2"`, run new workflows on v2 while old
443	//!    ones drain from v1, then decommission v1.
444	//! 3. **Check the CHANGELOG.** Any release whose transition behavior changed is flagged as
445	//!    replay-breaking.
446	//! 4. **Production path:** [Temporal Worker Versioning (Build IDs)](https://docs.temporal.io/workers#worker-versioning)
447	//!    is the long-term solution for zero-downtime updates; support is pending in the Rust SDK.
448	//!
449	//! # Links
450	//!
451	//! - [API reference (docs.rs)](https://docs.rs/paigasus-helikon-runtime-temporal)
452	//! - [Guide & concepts](https://smk1085.github.io/paigasus-helikon/) — see [Runtimes](https://smk1085.github.io/paigasus-helikon/concepts/runtimes.html)
453	//! - [Temporal documentation](https://docs.temporal.io)
454	//! - [Source & issues](https://github.com/SMK1085/paigasus-helikon)

# release-plz.toml — automated versioning, changelogs, GitHub releases.
# Reference: https://release-plz.dev/docs/config

[workspace]
# Makes the release PR run `cargo update` on `Cargo.lock`. It does not cascade
# version bumps. release-plz gives a dependent crate that has no commits of its
# own a patch bump only (release-plz#1599). For a breaking bump, see
# docs/runbooks/release-ascend.md, section "A breaking change in a crate with
# dependents" (SMA-838).
dependencies_update = true

# Force the scopeless release-PR title + commit (`chore: release`). release-plz's
# default SINGLE-crate template is `chore({package}): release {version}`, which uses
# the full package name (e.g. `paigasus-helikon`) as the Conventional-Commits scope —
# not in the convco/.versionrc + pr-title.yml allowlist (which uses short scopes like
# `facade`), so both the `commits` and `pr-title` gates reject it. The scopeless form
# matches the historical multi-crate release PRs and passes both. (Diagnosed on PR #58,
# the first facade-only release.)
pr_name = "chore: release"

# All library crates publish to crates.io (Stage 1 SMA-385 onward; the last
# stubs ascended in SMA-332/SMA-333). Remaining per-package overrides below
# are the only exceptions. See CLAUDE.md for the 4-step recipe a stub
# follows when it ascends.

[changelog]
sort_commits = "newest"

# Internal test members (three harnesses and one helper library): these four workspace members never publish.
# publish = false in each Cargo.toml and release = false here MUST move
# together.

# Internal cross-runtime HTTP wire-format conformance suite: boots BOTH the axum
# and actix runtimes and asserts byte/structural parity. Never published, so it
# carries the publish=false / release=false pair.
[[package]]
name = "paigasus-helikon-runtime-http-conformance"
publish = false
release = false

# Internal workspace-wide source lints (SMA-543). Never published, so it
# carries the same publish=false / release=false pair as the member above.
[[package]]
name = "paigasus-helikon-workspace-lints"
publish = false
release = false

# Internal cross-provider stream event-ordering conformance suite. Never
# published, so it carries the same publish=false / release=false pair as the
# members above.
[[package]]
name = "paigasus-helikon-provider-stream-conformance"
publish = false
release = false

# Internal test helpers shared by the core and runtime-tokio deferral tests
# (SMA-828). Never published, so it carries the same publish=false /
# release=false pair as the members above.
[[package]]
name = "paigasus-helikon-deferral-testkit"
publish = false
release = false

# Changelog

All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.0.0/),
and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

## [Unreleased]

## [0.8.3](https://github.com/SMK1085/paigasus-helikon/compare/paigasus-helikon-core-v0.8.2...paigasus-helikon-core-v0.8.3) - 2026-11-22

### Fixed

- *(providers)* SMA-854 send each anthropic text block at its own position ([#393](https://github.com/SMK1085/paigasus-helikon/pull/393))

## [0.8.2](https://github.com/SMK1085/paigasus-helikon/compare/paigasus-helikon-core-v0.8.1...paigasus-helikon-core-v0.8.2) - 2026-11-22

### Other

- *(providers)* SMA-567 extend the stream conformance suite to reasoning, parallel and zero-argument tool calls ([#392](https://github.com/SMK1085/paigasus-helikon/pull/392))

## [0.8.1](https://github.com/SMK1085/paigasus-helikon/compare/paigasus-helikon-core-v0.8.0...paigasus-helikon-core-v0.8.1) - 2026-11-21

### Fixed

- *(core)* SMA-621 refuse a turn with parallel blank call_id tool calls ([#378](https://github.com/SMK1085/paigasus-helikon/pull/378))

## [0.8.0](https://github.com/SMK1085/paigasus-helikon/compare/paigasus-helikon-core-v0.7.0...paigasus-helikon-core-v0.8.0) - 2026-11-21

### Added

- *(core)* [**breaking**] SMA-830 let a tool declare a provider tool type ([#374](https://github.com/SMK1085/paigasus-helikon/pull/374))

### Fixed

- *(providers)* SMA-827 round trip gemini thought signatures through a provider data part ([#373](https://github.com/SMK1085/paigasus-helikon/pull/373))

### Upgrade notes

- Build a `ToolDef` with `ToolDef::new` or `ToolDef::from_tool`. A struct literal and exhaustive destructuring no longer compile, because `ToolDef` is now `#[non_exhaustive]`.
- Upgrade `paigasus-helikon-core`, `paigasus-helikon` and the direct sibling dependencies together. Run `cargo tree -d` to check that the build has one copy of core.
- A tool wrapper must forward `Tool::provider_types`.
- The JSON of a `ToolDef` with no provider types does not change.

## [0.7.0](https://github.com/SMK1085/paigasus-helikon/compare/paigasus-helikon-core-v0.6.0...paigasus-helikon-core-v0.7.0) - 2026-11-20

### Fixed

- *(core)* SMA-810 give each handoff transfer call a tool result ([#358](https://github.com/SMK1085/paigasus-helikon/pull/358))

### Other

- *(deps)* [**breaking**] SMA-831 upgrade jiff to 1 ([#367](https://github.com/SMK1085/paigasus-helikon/pull/367))
- *(core)* SMA-828 share the deferral test helpers with runtime-tokio ([#366](https://github.com/SMK1085/paigasus-helikon/pull/366))
- *(core)* SMA-826 move the shared core test helpers into tests/common ([#359](https://github.com/SMK1085/paigasus-helikon/pull/359))

### Upgrade notes

- This release requires `jiff` 1. The `ts` fields of `SessionEvent` and the return value of `SessionEvent::ts()` now have the type `jiff::Timestamp` from jiff 1. A `Timestamp` from jiff 0.2 is a different type.
- If your code passes a `Timestamp` into a `SessionEvent`, or uses the value from `ts()` with jiff code, change your `jiff` requirement to `1`. Read the [jiff 1.0 changelog](https://github.com/BurntSushi/jiff/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md) for the APIs that jiff renamed.
- If your code uses only the constructors that set `ts` to the current time (for example `SessionEvent::user_message`) and does not read `ts`, it needs no change.
- Upgrade `paigasus-helikon-core` and `paigasus-helikon` to 0.7 together.
- The next patch release of each other `paigasus-helikon-*` crate requires core 0.7. If your `Cargo.toml` requires `paigasus-helikon-core` 0.6 directly, change it to `0.7` before you run `cargo update`. If you cannot upgrade core yet, keep the other `paigasus-helikon-*` crates at their current versions with `cargo update --precise`. Two copies of core in one build cause errors such as "trait not implemented". Run `cargo tree -d` to find the copies.
- The JSON format of a stored `SessionEvent` does not change. Session rows that an earlier version wrote stay readable.

## [0.6.0](https://github.com/SMK1085/paigasus-helikon/compare/paigasus-helikon-core-v0.5.21...paigasus-helikon-core-v0.6.0) - 2026-11-20

### Added

- *(core)* SMA-804 add a turn-boundary checkpoint to runcontext ([#346](https://github.com/SMK1085/paigasus-helikon/pull/346))
- *(core)* SMA-803 add deferred tool calls ([#344](https://github.com/SMK1085/paigasus-helikon/pull/344))

### Upgrade notes

- Once a host stores a `tool_deferred` event, it cannot roll back below this version, because an older reader cannot parse the row. Enable deferral only after every reader of the session store runs this version.

## [0.5.21](https://github.com/SMK1085/paigasus-helikon/compare/paigasus-helikon-core-v0.5.20...paigasus-helikon-core-v0.5.21) - 2026-11-12

### Other

# Agent Loop & State Machine

The agent loop is an explicit `enum LoopState`, driven by a pure `transition` function and surfaced as a typed `AgentEvent` stream. The state machine is *data*: `transition` is `async`-free, allocation-light, and never touches IO. An async driver runs the side effects between transitions. This is what makes the loop resumable — a durable runner can persist the state plus the conversation and rehydrate at any transition boundary.

All of this lives in [`paigasus-helikon-core`](https://github.com/SMK1085/paigasus-helikon/tree/main/crates/paigasus-helikon-core).

## The state machine

`LoopState` has one variant per high-level phase:

- `CallingModel { turn, usage }` — about to invoke the model for `turn`.
- `ExecutingTools { calls, turn, usage }` — the model requested tool calls; run them concurrently.
- `ApplyingHandoff { target, transcript, usage }` — delegate to another agent, threading the transcript.
- `Finalizing { turn, usage }` — a constrained turn that asks the model to emit the configured `output_type`.
- `RepairingOutput { turn, usage }` — the one allowed repair turn after a failed structured-output validation.
- `Compacting` — a reserved phase, not yet driven.
- `NeedsApproval { pending }` — terminal. The run stops here when a tool call is deferred. See [Deferred tool calls](./permissions-guardrails-hooks.md#deferred-tool-calls).
- `Done(FinalOutput)` — terminal success.
- `Failed(AgentError)` — terminal failure.

`transition` is the whole machine:

```rust
pub fn transition(
    state: &LoopState,
    input: TransitionInput,
    ctx: &TransitionCtx<'_>,
) -> TransitionOutcome;
```

It takes the current state, the most recent `TransitionInput` (`Start`, `ModelResponse`, or `ToolResults`), and a `TransitionCtx` (the tool defs, `ModelSettings`, `max_turns`, the accumulated `conversation`, the optional `OutputType`, and any handoff descriptors). It returns a `TransitionOutcome`:

```rust
pub struct TransitionOutcome {
    pub next_state: LoopState,
    pub events: Vec<AgentEvent>,
    pub next_action: NextAction,
    pub conversation_appends: Vec<Item>,
}
```

`next_action` tells the driver what side effect to run before the next step:

- `CallModel { request }` — call the model, feed the result back as `TransitionInput::ModelResponse`.
- `ExecuteTools { calls }` — fan out the tool calls, feed outcomes back as `TransitionInput::ToolResults`.
- `Handoff` — read the target/transcript from `ApplyingHandoff` and run the target agent.
- `Terminate` — the state is terminal; stop driving.

A typical run walks `CallingModel → ExecutingTools → CallingModel → … → Done`. Each tool round bumps `turn`; reaching `RunConfig::max_turns` fails the run with `AgentError::MaxTurnsExceeded`. With an `output_type` configured, the loop adds a `Finalizing` (and, on a validation miss, one `RepairingOutput`) turn before `Done`. See [Structured Output](./structured-output-builder.md) for that path.

## The event stream

`Agent::run` returns a `BoxStream<'static, AgentEvent>`. The outer `Result` only covers failure to *start* the stream; a fatal error mid-run arrives as an `AgentEvent::RunFailed` inside the stream, not as an `Err`.

`AgentEvent` is a single, serializable enum spanning lifecycle, raw deltas, post-aggregation semantic items, transitions, control signals, and terminal outcomes. The variants:

- Lifecycle: `RunStarted { agent }`, `TurnStarted { turn }`.
- Raw deltas (for low-latency UIs): `TokenDelta { text }`, `ReasoningDelta { text }`, `ToolCallDelta { call_id, name, args_delta }`.

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH CHANGES
The guard arm in the pure `transition` function is in the correct place, and the change is small. But the spec has no rollout section for the Temporal replay risk, and it says "no hand edit" to the CHANGELOG, which goes against the repo's documented upgrade rules. Two other paths still let a cut tool call run with `{}`. Also, the new typed error is not the only error that this root cause produces.

## Findings

### BLOCKER
None.

### MAJOR

- **The Temporal replay risk has no rollout plan, and §7 goes against the upgrade rules** - `transition` runs inside Temporal workflow code (`/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon-sma-864/crates/paigasus-helikon-runtime-temporal/src/workflow.rs:333`, `.../runtime-temporal/src/driver.rs:200`). A history where `call_model` returned `Length` + a tool call already holds an `invoke_tool` `ActivityTaskScheduled` event. With the new code, a replay gives `Finished` at that point, so Temporal raises a non-determinism error. The crate docs say: "Any release whose transition behavior changed is flagged as replay-breaking" (`.../runtime-temporal/src/lib.rs:330-336, 444-445`). Spec §7 says "A CHANGELOG is written by release-plz; no hand edit". But earlier releases added `### Upgrade notes` by hand (`/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon-sma-864/crates/paigasus-helikon-core/CHANGELOG.md:38-43, 57-64`), and the SMA-850 spec did the same (`/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon-sma-864/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-24-sma-850-claude-retired-model-ids-design.md:127`). | Why it matters: release-plz gives an additive `feat` on 0.x only a patch bump. A plain `cargo update` therefore puts this change into a running Temporal fleet without a runtime-temporal release. On a default configuration, a workflow that hits the error stays stuck. | Suggested fix: Add a "Rollout" section. Add an `### Upgrade notes` entry under `## [Unreleased]` in the core CHANGELOG, and also in the runtime-temporal CHANGELOG. The entry must say "replay-breaking for in-flight runs" and tell users to drain or use a blue-green task queue. Remove the "no hand edit" sentence.

- **A truncated stream (no `Finish`) still runs a cut call with `{}`** - Core's contract says that a provider "MUST NOT emit [Finish] on truncation with no stop reason observed, on cancellation, or after a mid-stream error" (`/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon-sma-864/crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/model.rs:66-68`). But `ModelTurnAccumulator` sets `finish_reason` to `Stop` by default (`.../core/src/model.rs:694`), so a turn with no `Finish` looks the same as a clean stop. The OpenAI Chat test `truncated_stream_flushes_name_but_emits_no_finish` shows a named call with empty arguments and no `Finish` (`/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon-sma-864/crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-openai/src/backend/chat.rs:1301-1316`). LiteLLM does the same (`.../providers-litellm/src/stream.rs:733-738`). Core then changes `""` to `{}` and the loop runs the call. Spec §2 says `Stop` "keeps today's behavior". | Why it matters: This is the same hazard that SMA-864 fixes, through a different path. The spec's intent ("the model did not mean that input") is not met for a stream that the server closes before the end. | Suggested fix: Choose one, in writing. (a) Extend the guard: record whether a `Finish` came, for example with a `finish_observed: bool` on `ModelTurn` (`#[non_exhaustive]`, serde default `true` so that Temporal payloads stay readable), and block tool calls when it is `false`. (b) Put it in §5 as a non-goal with a linked Linear follow-up issue. If you choose (b), add `#[non_exhaustive]` to the variant now, so a later `Option<FinishReason>` field does not break callers.

- **`model_context_window_exceeded` maps to `Other` and gets past the deny-list** - Bedrock maps `StopReason::ModelContextWindowExceeded` to `Other("model_context_window_exceeded")`, and a test locks this in (`/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon-sma-864/crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-bedrock/src/stream.rs:415-417, 815-827`). Anthropic sends the same wire string through its catch-all (`.../providers-anthropic/src/stream.rs:488-490`). This stop reason cuts the output exactly as `max_tokens` does. | Why it matters: In an agent loop the context grows on every turn. This stop reason is therefore more likely in agent runs than in single calls, and a cut `tool_use` block then runs with `{}`. This does not reopen the deny-list decision. It is a gap in what the list catches. | Suggested fix: Map `model_context_window_exceeded` to `FinishReason::Length` in the Anthropic and Bedrock translators, and change the Bedrock test. Either list this as one named exception to "No provider changes", or file a linked follow-up issue.

- **One root cause gives two different public errors** - When a cut call carries partial JSON, `build_items` fails (`/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon-sma-864/crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/model.rs:650-655`) before `transition` runs. The local driver then fails with `AgentError::Other("invalid tool args …")` (`.../core/src/agent.rs:1505-1513`), and Temporal does the same (`.../runtime-temporal/src/activities.rs:110-112`). This is the common case for every provider that streams JSON arguments: Anthropic, Bedrock, OpenAI Chat, OpenAI Responses and LiteLLM. Spec §5 names only OpenAI. Only two cases reach the new guard: a call with no argument bytes, and complete calls with `Length`. | Why it matters: The variant's doc reads as *the* signal for "the turn was cut". A caller that matches `ToolCallsNotRun` to raise `max_tokens` will miss most real cases. | Suggested fix: Either (a) add `ModelTurnAccumulator::finish_reason(&self) -> &FinishReason` (additive), read it before `finish()` in `agent.rs`, and map a reassembly error on a `Length`/`ContentFilter` turn to `ToolCallsNotRun`. Or (b) keep the current scope, fix §5 to name all five providers, and write in the variant doc and the book that a cut call can also fail as `AgentError::Other`.

- **The Temporal half of the "covers both runners" claim has no test** - §4 chooses `transition` because "one change covers both runners", but all the tests in §6 are core tests. `DurableDriver` is pure and has a unit-test module (`/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon-sma-864/crates/paigasus-helikon-runtime-temporal/src/driver.rs:396` onward, which already builds `ModelTurn::new(.., FinishReason::ToolCalls)` at lines 568, 651). | Why it matters: The main design reason has no test. A later change in the driver (for example, a pre-check before `transition`) could silently skip the guard. | Suggested fix: Add a driver unit test. Feed `apply_model` a `ModelTurn` with `Length` + one `ToolCall`, then assert that `next_effect()` gives `DriverEffect::Finished` with `RunStatusPayload::AgentFailed(ErrorKindPayload::Other { .. })` and never `ExecuteTools`.

### MINOR

- **The event contract leaves `ToolCallItem` unclear** - §2 lists `MessageOutput` and `RunFailed`. It does not say "no `ToolCallItem`". The handoff arm does emit `ToolCallItem` for transfer calls (`/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon-sma-864/crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/loop_state.rs:308-312`), so a builder could copy that. `SessionRecorder` adds a synthesized `tool_returned` for each unmatched `ToolCallItem` (`.../core/src/session.rs:1453-1479`). So this choice changes what the session stores. Clients already got `ToolCallDelta` events while the stream ran (`.../core/src/agent.rs:1478-1487`). AG-UI closes an open call on `RunFailed` (`.../runtime-agentcore/src/agui/map.rs:1528-1550`), and Anthropic ignores an orphan position part on the next request (`.../providers-anthropic/src/translate/request.rs:2414-2434`). | Suggested fix: Write "emits no `ToolCallItem`". Add a test which shows that the session holds the assistant message and no `tool_call`/`tool_returned`.

- **The `Display` text has no length limit** - `{tool_names:?}` is not capped. The turn is at `max_tokens` by definition, and tool names are model output. The same crate already caps such lists at 8 names of 64 characters each (`format_blank_names`, `/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon-sma-864/crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/model.rs:784-798`, SMA-621). The text goes to `RunFailed`, the span status, AG-UI `RUN_ERROR`, the Temporal payload, and through `AgentAsTool` to a parent model (`.../core/src/agent_as_tool.rs:191`). | Suggested fix: Use the same cap in the `#[error]` text. Keep the full `Vec` in the field.

- **"In call order" is unclear** - Core sorts tool calls by `call_id` (`BTreeMap`, `/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon-sma-864/crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/model.rs:577, 624, 676`), not in stream order. | Suggested fix: Write "in item order (sorted by `call_id`)". Also think about a `call_ids` field, so clients can match the error to the `ToolCallDelta` events they already got.

- **The variant doc is not correct for all providers** - "makes its tool calls unreliable" is false for Gemini, where function calls arrive whole (`/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon-sma-864/crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-gemini/src/stream.rs:47-58`). It is also false for OpenAI Responses calls that `output_item.done` closed (`.../providers-openai/src/backend/responses.rs:564-581`). Under the turn-as-unit rule, a Gemini `MAX_TOKENS` turn with one complete call also fails. | Suggested fix: Use the doc text "the model turn did not end cleanly, so the loop did not run its tool calls". Write the accepted false positive in §2.

- **The cut turn's usage is lost** - This turn is the most costly kind (it ran to `max_tokens`). `Failed` carries no usage. The Temporal `DurableRunOutcome.usage` leaves out this turn (`/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon-sma-864/crates/paigasus-helikon-runtime-temporal/src/driver.rs:204-206, 384-394`). The run span records usage only on `RunCompleted` and `RunDeferred` (`.../core/src/agent.rs:1410-1418`). The same thing happens when a `RepairingOutput` turn fails, so §5 is consistent. | Suggested fix: Think about a `usage: TokenUsage` field on the variant. If you do not add one, write that only the per-turn `gen_ai.chat` span (`.../core/src/agent.rs:1520-1521`) holds this usage.

- **Add `#[non_exhaustive]` to the variant** - This lets you add `call_ids`, `usage` or an `Option<FinishReason>` later without a breaking change. Code outside core then cannot build the variant. No crate needs to, because Temporal maps it to `Other`.

- **The test location goes against the convention** - §6 says "Unit test in `loop_state.rs`". That file has no test module. The pure `transition` tests live in `/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon-sma-864/crates/paigasus-helikon-core/tests/transition_unit.rs`, which already imports `FinishReason` and `HandoffDef` (lines 4-8, 652-656). | Suggested fix: Name that file.

- **Name the book page** - `/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon-sma-864/docs/book/src/concepts/agent-loop.md:49` describes the run walk and its failure modes. It must get a sentence about this rule. The core README has no text about loop behavior or error variants (checked), so it needs no edit. | Suggested fix: Replace the "if one exists" condition with that path.

- **LiteLLM and Bedrock map guardrails in different ways** - LiteLLM maps `guardrail_intervened` to `Other` (`/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon-sma-864/crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-litellm/src/stream.rs:1023-1036`). Bedrock maps `GuardrailIntervened` to `ContentFilter` (`.../providers-bedrock/src/stream.rs:410-413`). So a call that a LiteLLM guardrail cuts still runs. | Suggested fix: Map it to `ContentFilter`, or put it in the same follow-up issue as the context-window mapping.

- **Some tests are missing** - (1) A mixed turn with two complete calls and one cut call runs no call. §2 states this rule, but §6 has no test for it. (2) A tool call with `Other("function_call")` still runs. This is the case that §4 uses to reject the allow-list, so it is a better regression test than `Stop` alone. (3) Assistant text + a cut call: `MessageOutput` comes before `RunFailed`. (4) The e2e test asserts that `collect()` returns `RunError::Agent(AgentError::ToolCallsNotRun { .. })` through the failure slot (`/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon-sma-864/crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/agent.rs:1583-1594`), and that `MockTool::invocations()` is empty (`.../core/tests/common/mod.rs:79-81`).

### QUESTIONS

- A handoff transfer tool takes no arguments (`/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon-sma-864/crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/loop_state.rs:745-757`), so a cut transfer call still has its full meaning. Do you intend to fail the run instead of handing off? The turn-as-unit rule permits this, but §2 gives "a transfer call can be cut too" as the reason, and that reason does not apply here.
- OpenAI Responses maps `Status::Incomplete` with no `incomplete_details` to `Length` (`/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon-sma-864/crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-openai/src/backend/responses.rs:787`), so the guard blocks it. Do you intend this?
- On Temporal, `ToolCallsNotRun` becomes `AgentError::Other` (`/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon-sma-864/crates/paigasus-helikon-runtime-temporal/src/error.rs:126-128, 153-155`), so a caller cannot match the variant there. Is this acceptable for the first release? If a typed payload comes later, the CLAUDE.md rule "bump core in the same PR when a crate uses new core API" applies.
- A session stored before the upgrade can hold a deferred call from a `Length` turn. On resume, `run_resolved_calls` runs it without `transition` (`/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon-sma-864/crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/agent.rs:1171-1179`). A human approval covers this case. Should the upgrade note mention it?
- If the no-`Finish` truncation and the context-window mapping stay out of scope, which Linear issue tracks them?

## What's good

- The guard sits in the pure `transition` function. That is one change, it reaches both drivers (only `agent.rs:1206` and `runtime-temporal/src/driver.rs:200` call `transition`; `control.rs` and `agui/map.rs` only mention it in comments), and you can test it with no async code. I confirmed the claims in the rejected-alternatives list: OpenAI Chat maps `function_call` to `Other` (`providers-openai/src/backend/chat.rs:375`).
- I confirmed that the semver claim is correct. `AgentError` is `#[non_exhaustive]`, and no crate outside core matches it without a wildcard. The Temporal mapping uses `_` (`runtime-temporal/src/error.rs:126`), the HTTP and AgentCore runtimes do not match on variants, and no core test or eval fixture feeds `Length`/`ContentFilter` with a tool call today.
- The turn-as-unit rule, the explicit order (after max-turns and before the handoff check), and the `Stop` regression test that stops a later change to an allow-list are clear and easy to test. Keep them.

- **The event contract leaves `ToolCallItem` unclear** - §2 lists `MessageOutput` and `RunFailed`. It does not say "no `ToolCallItem`". The handoff arm does emit `ToolCallItem` for transfer calls (`/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon-sma-864/crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/loop_state.rs:308-312`), so a builder could copy that. `SessionRecorder` adds a synthesized `tool_returned` for each unmatched `ToolCallItem` (`.../core/src/session.rs:1453-1479`). So this choice changes what the session stores. Clients already got `ToolCallDelta` events while the stream ran (`.../core/src/agent.rs:1478-1487`). AG-UI closes an open call on `RunFailed` (`.../runtime-agentcore/src/agui/map.rs:1528-1550`), and Anthropic ignores an orphan position part on the next request (`.../providers-anthropic/src/translate/request.rs:2414-2434`). | Suggested fix: Write "emits no `ToolCallItem`". Add a test which shows that the session holds the assistant message and no `tool_call`/`tool_returned`.

- **The `Display` text has no length limit** - `{tool_names:?}` is not capped. The turn is at `max_tokens` by definition, and tool names are model output. The same crate already caps such lists at 8 names of 64 characters each (`format_blank_names`, `/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon-sma-864/crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/model.rs:784-798`, SMA-621). The text goes to `RunFailed`, the span status, AG-UI `RUN_ERROR`, the Temporal payload, and through `AgentAsTool` to a parent model (`.../core/src/agent_as_tool.rs:191`). | Suggested fix: Use the same cap in the `#[error]` text. Keep the full `Vec` in the field.

- **"In call order" is unclear** - Core sorts tool calls by `call_id` (`BTreeMap`, `/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon-sma-864/crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/model.rs:577, 624, 676`), not in stream order. | Suggested fix: Write "in item order (sorted by `call_id`)". Also think about a `call_ids` field, so clients can match the error to the `ToolCallDelta` events they already got.

- **The variant doc is not correct for all providers** - "makes its tool calls unreliable" is false for Gemini, where function calls arrive whole (`/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon-sma-864/crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-gemini/src/stream.rs:47-58`). It is also false for OpenAI Responses calls that `output_item.done` closed (`.../providers-openai/src/backend/responses.rs:564-581`). Under the turn-as-unit rule, a Gemini `MAX_TOKENS` turn with one complete call also fails. | Suggested fix: Use the doc text "the model turn did not end cleanly, so the loop did not run its tool calls". Write the accepted false positive in §2.

- **The cut turn's usage is lost** - This turn is the most costly kind (it ran to `max_tokens`). `Failed` carries no usage. The Temporal `DurableRunOutcome.usage` leaves out this turn (`/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon-sma-864/crates/paigasus-helikon-runtime-temporal/src/driver.rs:204-206, 384-394`). The run span records usage only on `RunCompleted` and `RunDeferred` (`.../core/src/agent.rs:1410-1418`). The same thing happens when a `RepairingOutput` turn fails, so §5 is consistent. | Suggested fix: Think about a `usage: TokenUsage` field on the variant. If you do not add one, write that only the per-turn `gen_ai.chat` span (`.../core/src/agent.rs:1520-1521`) holds this usage.

- **Add `#[non_exhaustive]` to the variant** - This lets you add `call_ids`, `usage` or an `Option<FinishReason>` later without a breaking change. Code outside core then cannot build the variant. No crate needs to, because Temporal maps it to `Other`.

- **The test location goes against the convention** - §6 says "Unit test in `loop_state.rs`". That file has no test module. The pure `transition` tests live in `/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon-sma-864/crates/paigasus-helikon-core/tests/transition_unit.rs`, which already imports `FinishReason` and `HandoffDef` (lines 4-8, 652-656). | Suggested fix: Name that file.

- **Name the book page** - `/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon-sma-864/docs/book/src/concepts/agent-loop.md:49` describes the run walk and its failure modes. It must get a sentence about this rule. The core README has no text about loop behavior or error variants (checked), so it needs no edit. | Suggested fix: Replace the "if one exists" condition with that path.

- **LiteLLM and Bedrock map guardrails in different ways** - LiteLLM maps `guardrail_intervened` to `Other` (`/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon-sma-864/crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-litellm/src/stream.rs:1023-1036`). Bedrock maps `GuardrailIntervened` to `ContentFilter` (`.../providers-bedrock/src/stream.rs:410-413`). So a call that a LiteLLM guardrail cuts still runs. | Suggested fix: Map it to `ContentFilter`, or put it in the same follow-up issue as the context-window mapping.

- **Some tests are missing** - (1) A mixed turn with two complete calls and one cut call runs no call. §2 states this rule, but §6 has no test for it. (2) A tool call with `Other("function_call")` still runs. This is the case that §4 uses to reject the allow-list, so it is a better regression test than `Stop` alone. (3) Assistant text + a cut call: `MessageOutput` comes before `RunFailed`. (4) The e2e test asserts that `collect()` returns `RunError::Agent(AgentError::ToolCallsNotRun { .. })` through the failure slot (`/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon-sma-864/crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/agent.rs:1583-1594`), and that `MockTool::invocations()` is empty (`.../core/tests/common/mod.rs:79-81`).

### QUESTIONS

- A handoff transfer tool takes no arguments (`/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon-sma-864/crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/loop_state.rs:745-757`), so a cut transfer call still has its full meaning. Do you intend to fail the run instead of handing off? The turn-as-unit rule permits this, but §2 gives "a transfer call can be cut too" as the reason, and that reason does not apply here.
- OpenAI Responses maps `Status::Incomplete` with no `incomplete_details` to `Length` (`/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon-sma-864/crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-openai/src/backend/responses.rs:787`), so the guard blocks it. Do you intend this?
- On Temporal, `ToolCallsNotRun` becomes `AgentError::Other` (`/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon-sma-864/crates/paigasus-helikon-runtime-temporal/src/error.rs:126-128, 153-155`), so a caller cannot match the variant there. Is this acceptable for the first release? If a typed payload comes later, the CLAUDE.md rule "bump core in the same PR when a crate uses new core API" applies.
- A session stored before the upgrade can hold a deferred call from a `Length` turn. On resume, `run_resolved_calls` runs it without `transition` (`/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon-sma-864/crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/agent.rs:1171-1179`). A human approval covers this case. Should the upgrade note mention it?
- If the no-`Finish` truncation and the context-window mapping stay out of scope, which Linear issue tracks them?

## What's good

- The guard sits in the pure `transition` function. That is one change, it reaches both drivers (only `agent.rs:1206` and `runtime-temporal/src/driver.rs:200` call `transition`; `control.rs` and `agui/map.rs` only mention it in comments), and you can test it with no async code. I confirmed the claims in the rejected-alternatives list: OpenAI Chat maps `function_call` to `Other` (`providers-openai/src/backend/chat.rs:375`).
- I confirmed that the semver claim is correct. `AgentError` is `#[non_exhaustive]`, and no crate outside core matches it without a wildcard. The Temporal mapping uses `_` (`runtime-temporal/src/error.rs:126`), the HTTP and AgentCore runtimes do not match on variants, and no core test or eval fixture feeds `Length`/`ContentFilter` with a tool call today.
- The turn-as-unit rule, the explicit order (after max-turns and before the handoff check), and the `Stop` regression test that stops a later change to an allow-list are clear and easy to test. Keep them.
